channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Biocompatible piezoionic eutectogel sensor for self-powered physiological monitoring
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77390-7

Piezoionics enables effective mechanical-to-electrical conversion in self-powered bioelectronics. Here, the authors develop a biocompatible eutectogel with tailored hydrogen-bonded networks, achieving excellent piezoionic properties for high-fidelity physiological signal monitoring.
item.dc:title: Biocompatible piezoionic eutectogel sensor for self-powered physiological monitoring

item.title: The phosphorus analogues of diazomethane and isomeric diazirine
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78120-9

Diazo compounds and isomeric diazirines have been used as powerful reagents in synthetic chemistry since the first discovery of the parent molecules diazomethane and isomeric 3H-diazirine, but little is known about their phosphorus analogues. Here, the authors report the preparation and characterization of methyleneaminophosphinidene and 3H-azaphosphirine.
item.dc:title: The phosphorus analogues of diazomethane and isomeric diazirine

item.title: Expandable and scalable production of cellulose nanofibrils via highly efficient swelling-modification in deep eutectic solvent
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77866-6

Deep eutectic solvents enable sustainable, scalable production of cellulose nanofibers, but current systems are acidic, degrading the cellulose. Here, the authors use a pH buffering deep eutectic solvent to obtain cellulose nanofibrils with high aspect ratios and degrees of polymerisation.
item.dc:title: Expandable and scalable production of cellulose nanofibrils via highly efficient swelling-modification in deep eutectic solvent

item.title: Efficient field-free magnetization switching through orbital-current-enhanced magnon torque
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77984-1

Orbital currents have been shown to allow for efficient switching of magnetization. Here, Shi et al. build on this point, demonstrating how spin and orbital currents in RuO2 can jointly excite magnons in an adjacent magnetic insulator, NiO, leading to enhanced magnon torque efficiency and field-free magnetization switching.
item.dc:title: Efficient field-free magnetization switching through orbital-current-enhanced magnon torque

item.title: Ghost Neuron preparation unlocks high-resolution structural mapping of intracellular architecture in axons
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77741-4

The authors introduce Ghost Neuron, a cryo-EM preparation that improves visualization of neuronal projections and maps macromolecular structures within axons at near-atomic resolution.
item.dc:title: Ghost Neuron preparation unlocks high-resolution structural mapping of intracellular architecture in axons

item.title: Solid–vapor synthesis of dynamic crystalline one-dimensional supramolecular polymers from amorphous macrocycles
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78015-9

Crystalline supramolecular polymers (CSPs) possess ordered polymeric structures for establishing structure–function relationships but most reported CSPs lack dynamic and responsive characteristics intrinsic to supramolecular polymers. Herein the authors report a highly dynamic CSP via a unique solid–vapor host–guest-driven synthesis.
item.dc:title: Solid–vapor synthesis of dynamic crystalline one-dimensional supramolecular polymers from amorphous macrocycles
